title: Navigation API: make the "signals to the user … via … assistive technology … that the navigation is finished" behavior for intercepted navigations normative

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
## Background

When a cross-document navigation completes, browsers signal completion through browser UI (spinner stops) and through platform accessibility APIs, so screen readers are given the chance to notify the user that the page is loaded and ready for interaction.

[A stated design goal of the Navigation API](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api#accessibility-technology-announcements) was that intercepted same-document navigations would get the same treatment, so that well-behaved SPAs are announced like MPAs without per-app ARIA workarounds.

Today the spec expresses this only in the [non-normative domintro for `navigateEvent.intercept()`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#navigation-api:~:text=e.g.%2C%20via%20a%20loading%20spinner%20UI%2C%20or%20assistive%20technology):

> After it settles, the browser signals to the user (e.g., via a loading spinner UI, or assistive technology) that the navigation is finished.

There is no corresponding step in the normative algorithms. The only normative user-facing behavior at settle time is *potentially reset the focus*. As a result, engines have diverged.

In testing [this example](https://gist.github.com/WestonThayer/57b1e80d0f8985438565eb60bcddd5d0) for what screen readers announce when a link is invoked (apologies, I've omitted Orca and the mobile screen readers):

| | NVDA 2026.1.1 | JAWS 2026 | Narrator (Windows 11) | macOS VoiceOver (Tahoe) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome 151 | *silence* | *announces the link invoked, then info overview about the new page* | "{document.title}, {document.title} has finished loading" | *Untested, Chrome generally doesn't work well with VoiceOver* |
| Firefox 153 | "visited same page, {document.title}" | {document.title}, {document.title}  document" | "{document.title}, {document.title}" | *silence* |
| Safari 26.3 | N/A | N/A | N/A | *silence* |

Chromium fires a document load-complete accessibility event when the intercept handlers settle ([`NavigateEvent` finish steps call `HandleLoadComplete`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/navigation_api/navigate_event.cc); implemented in [CL 3462694](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/3462694), 2022) which explains some support there. Comments note that NVDA isn't listening for that event, so fix might be on their side (I filed https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/20729).

I'm not sure how Firefox supports, but there appears to be some support as legacy navigations via the History API are silent in my testing.

Safari appears to have no support (I filed https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=322426).

So two of three engines ship a completion signal and interoperate reasonably; the third ships none.

## Design history
 
The WICG explainer had a dedicated ["Accessibility technology announcements" section](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api#accessibility-technology-announcements) promising that a converted navigation "will be communicated to accessibility technology in the same way as a cross-document one." See also WICG/navigation-api#25 (announcements) and WICG/navigation-api#190 (focus management). That repo is now archived, and when the API was upstreamed in #8502 this intent came along only as the domintro sentence above.

## Proposal

I'm out of my depth here, but generally adding normative language to the spec for notifications to assistive technologies upon `intercept()` completions.
